en: The Buddha Preaches the Sūtra on Receiving Dust.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master An Shigao of Parthia during the Later Han Dynasty.
Thus have I heard: At one time, the Buddha was staying at Śrāvastī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍada’s Park.
The Buddha addressed them, saying:
"O Bhikṣus! The Bhikṣus replied: [as instructed].
"I shall receive the teaching," he replied,
and listened to the Buddha.
The Buddha said:

“Monks! When ordinary people engage in a single practice that causes them to be defiled by the dust of the senses, they become deluded and sorrowful, sinking into the boundless depths; I see that they shall not attain the unsurpassed path of auspiciousness.”
Just as a man who desires to see the form of a woman, because he is a person of beautiful appearance, becomes stained, intoxicated, greedy, defiled, deluded, attached, settled, and possessed by it.
Because of the words of the courtesan, he has for a long time run back and forth, undergoing diligent suffering.

His ears constantly desire to hear the sound of the courtesan; his nose desires to smell her fragrance; his tongue desires to obtain her flavor; his body desires to experience her smoothness. For this reason, he has for a long time run back and forth, coming and going to undergo suffering.
Therefore, one should not be defiled or deluded by female forms, sounds, fragrances, tastes, or tactile sensations; one should be aware of this.
Furthermore, O bhikṣus!

Ordinary people who practice the Dharma allow themselves to be defiled by sensory dust; deluded and filled with sorrow, they sink without end, and I see that they shall not attain the path of unsurpassed auspiciousness.

Just as a courtesan desires to see the form of a man, so too does a woman of beautiful complexion, for the sake of a man’s form, become stained, intoxicated, greedy, defiled, deluded, attached, settled, and subject to experience; she runs and hastens for a long time, coming and going while undergoing suffering.

The ears constantly desire to hear the voices of men; the nose desires to smell their fragrance; the tongue desires to obtain their flavors; and the body desires to experience their smoothness. For this reason, one runs about for a long time, coming and going, and undergoes suffering.
"Therefore, one should not be defiled or deluded by the forms, sounds, odors, tastes, and tactile sensations of a noble person; one should be aware of this.
When the Buddha had finished speaking these words, they all received them with joy and put them into practice.
The Sūtra on Receiving Dust Spoken by the Buddha.
